title: P@x memory entry
description: One entry of the assistant's local memory (AI control layer, section 16.1), as stored in <store>/memory/entries/<id>.json. An entry is data and never authority: nothing in it can lower an action's class, stand in for a confirmation or act as a standing approval, and no property of this document is read by the policy engine. The loader in services/tur-pax-memory is authoritative. It also enforces what this schema cannot express: sizes are counted in bytes, not characters; text fields hold no control characters (the entry text may hold line breaks and tabs); a service name has at least two dot-separated elements; the arguments of a procedure step are at most 8192 bytes as JSON; updated_at is not before created_at; and the identifier equals the file name.

timestamp.description: Whole seconds since the Unix epoch, UTC. At most the last second of the year 9999.

provenance.description: Where the entry came from. For an entry taken from content, the origin is itself content and is not trusted.

origin.description: Where it came from, in words: a conversation, a window title, a file path, a tool name.

task.description: The task during which the entry was recorded.

step.description: One step of a saved procedure: a tool and a template for its arguments. The template is stored as written and is not interpreted.

service.description: The D-Bus name of the service that owns the tool.

procedure.description: A named sequence of steps recorded from a task the user accepted. It is a note of what worked, not a permission: replaying it is an ordinary task and every step goes through the policy engine again.

id.description: The entry identifier: m- and 8 to 16 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

kind.description: stated: the user said it. observed: recorded by the assistant from its own completed actions. procedure: steps saved from a task the user accepted. from_content: taken from something the assistant read.

state.description: active: the entry can be recalled. pending: the entry was taken from content and waits for the user's confirmation; it is never recalled.

trust.description: Follows from the kind and cannot be raised: stated is user_stated, observed and procedure are assistant_observed, from_content is untrusted, also after the user confirmed that it may be kept. A file whose trust does not follow from its kind is rejected.

text.description: What was remembered. Refused at the point of writing if it looks like a secret.

confirmed_at.description: When the user confirmed an entry taken from content.

oneOf.description: Taken from content, waiting for the user.
Taken from content and confirmed by the user. It stays untrusted.
